target.title: feat(android): add Wear real-time Talk controls
target.body:
[AI-assisted]
## What Problem This Solves

The Wear OS companion from #108997 can proxy messages and threads through the paired Android phone, but voice remains fragmented: one-shot dictation, continuous real-time conversation, agent audio, thinking state, and connection controls do not yet form one watch-first flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR depends on #108997 and extends the canonical WearProtocol and phone proxy merged in #109341 instead of keeping a parallel bridge. Real-Time Talk is bound to the requesting Wear node, audio frames are bounded on exact Data Layer paths, and the phone remains the authenticated Gateway and security boundary.

## User Impact

The watch now centers voice on one large microphone: hold to dictate one message, tap for continuous Live Talk, and double tap to open the thread. Live transcripts, agent thinking, playback, interruption, gateway controls, and light/dark visual states stay usable on the round display without placing Gateway credentials on the watch.

## Evidence

> [!NOTE]
> ### Validation
>
> - [x] `./gradlew :wear-shared:ktlintCheck :wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest :wear:ktlintCheck :wear:testDebugUnitTest :app:ktlintCheck` — passed
> - [x] `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` — passed
> - [x] `./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` — passed
> - [x] `./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug :wear:lintDebug :app:assemblePlayDebug :app:assembleThirdPartyDebug :app:lintPlayDebug :app:lintThirdPartyDebug` — passed
> - [x] `vitest run realtime-voice-provider gateway-protocol talk-session talk-realtime-relay session-runtime` — 8 files and 366 tests passed
> - [x] `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json && tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json` — no-emit type checks passed

> [!TIP]
> ### Real Behavior Proof
>
> A physical paired phone and Wear OS watch exercised the final voice-first UI and continuous Talk transport end to end.
>
> - [x] **Environment:** Physical round Wear OS watch paired to the OpenClaw Android app over Wear Data Layer and an authenticated phone Gateway session.
> - [x] **Security boundary:** The watch exchanges bounded protocol messages and PCM frames only with the paired phone; Gateway credentials and identity remain phone-side.
> - [x] **Live Talk result:** Start, listening, thinking, agent playback, interruption, and stop remain in the watch flow.
> - [x] **Dictation result:** One-message speech input remains available from the same large microphone without replacing Live Talk.
> - [x] **Thread result:** Conversation updates stay current and the thread remains reachable by the home double-tap gesture.
> - [x] **Physical watch result:** The final implementation is captured in the two public physical-watch proof videos below.

target.title: feat: align native macOS chat with the web chat capability set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native macOS chat lags the web Control UI chat in day-to-day capabilities, even though much of the machinery already exists. Several fully implemented shared surfaces were unreachable on macOS: the sessions manager sheet (`ChatSessionsSheet`) was dead code with no trigger anywhere, assistant reasoning/tool traces were hard-disabled, talk mode / voice notes / per-message Listen were implemented in `OpenClawChatUI` and wired on iOS but never injected by the macOS host, and the mac transport silently dropped the `verboseLevel` session setting. The composer also lacked three everyday web-chat features: input history recall, reply/quote, and per-session draft retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligning the native macOS chat with the web chat's capability set, preferring host wiring of existing shared code over new surface area. Two staged commits:

**1. `feat(macos)` — host wiring (mac app + minimal shared passthroughs)**
- Sessions manager reachable: **Sessions…** toolbar action + Shift-Cmd-S opens the Active/Archived manager (gateway search, rename, pin, archive, restore). The unreachable `showSessions` state in `OpenClawChatView` is deleted.
- Assistant reasoning & tool activity visible in the full window, with a persisted toggle (`openclaw.webchat.showAssistantTrace`, default on; compact panel stays minimal).
- New `MacChatSurface` observing wrapper bridges live state into the once-constructed `NSHostingController` hierarchy: talk control (bridged to the existing `TalkModeController`/`AppStateStore` paths without touching the menu-bar overlay), voice-note recording (blocked while Talk Mode owns mic capture), per-message **Listen** via gateway `tts.speak` bound to the transport's server lease with local synthesis fallback (mirrors the iOS client), and starter prompts on empty sessions.
- `MacGatewayChatTransport` now forwards `verboseLevel` in `sessions.patch` instead of dropping it.

**2. `feat(clients)` — shared composer parity (macOS + iOS)**
- Input history: Up/Down recall of prior inputs (session-scoped, cap 100, transcript-seeded plus locally sent slash commands, draft stash/restore, Escape cancels), mirroring `ui/src/pages/chat/input-history.ts` semantics. Slash-panel navigation keeps priority.
- Reply/quote: context-menu Reply → cancellable composer chip → outgoing message prepends the exact web blockquote format from `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` (`prependReplyQuote`, same Markdown escape set, 500/120 UTF-16 truncation limits), so transcripts look identical across surfaces.
- Per-session drafts: composer text survives session switches (in-memory; revision-guarded so races with in-flight sends cannot eat newer text). Accepted tradeoffs vs web (no cross-launch persistence, no attachment drafts) are noted in code comments.

All shared-package API changes are additive with defaulted parameters; iOS call sites compile unchanged.

## User Impact

macOS chat gains: full session management (rename/archive/restore/search), visible reasoning and tool activity with a toggle, talk mode + voice notes + read-aloud in the chat surfaces, starter prompts, `/verbose` that actually sticks, Up/Down input history, reply-with-quote, and drafts that survive session switching. iOS inherits the composer features. Docs updated: `docs/platforms/mac/webchat.md`.

## Evidence

- `swift build --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --target OpenClawChatUI` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --parallel` — 48/48 XCTest; Swift Testing 853/856 with 3 pre-existing issues in untouched surfaces (see below)
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --configuration release` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel` — 1280/1280 pass
- Gateway contracts verified in-repo: `tts.speak` (`src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts`), `sessions.patch` `verboseLevel` (`src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts:465`)
- Quote format verified against `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` `prependReplyQuote` + escape regex
- Pre-existing OpenClawKitTests failures (not touched by this PR, reproduced identically on two independent checkouts including one with composer-only changes and one with host-only changes): stale pairing-copy expectations (`GatewayErrorsTests.swift:59`, copy changed in 551c9637d8a3), watch legacy payload decode (`WatchCommandsTests.swift:74`, compat added in ec65e10df7fc and lost by a later watch commit), and a load-flaky attachment timeout (passes 9/10 isolated). CI does not run this suite; follow-up task filed to repair it and add coverage.

target.title: fix(skills): pass ownerHandle in ClawHub bulk verdict targets to resolve ambiguous slugs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `skills.securityVerdicts` returns `skill_not_found` for installed owner-qualified ClawHub skills with ambiguous bare slugs (e.g., `@anysearch-ai/anysearch`). The bulk verdict API receives only `{ registry, slug, version }` without `ownerHandle`, so ambiguous slugs cannot be resolved. Meanwhile, owner-qualified single-skill verify succeeds.

Fixes #108654

## Why This Change Was Made

`collectClawHubVerdictTargets()` now reads `link.ownerHandle` from the linked ClawHub origin/status metadata and includes it in bulk verdict targets when present. `fetchOpenClawSkillSecurityVerdicts()` forwards `ownerHandle` to the ClawHub API call. target.title: fix(elevenlabs): treat blank env API keys as unconfigured
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` / `XI_API_KEY` environment values are truthy strings, so the ElevenLabs providers treated them as real credentials:

- `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured` returned `true` when `XI_API_KEY="  "`, so auto-selection could pick the realtime provider and only fail later at connection time.
- `transcribeElevenLabsAudio` skipped its `ElevenLabs API key missing` guard and sent the speech-to-text request with an empty `xi-api-key` header, surfacing as a confusing upstream 401 instead of a clear local configuration error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-file key path already normalizes blanks (`normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`), and the profile fallback already trims (`resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`). Only the raw env fallbacks bypassed normalization. This routes them (plus the request-level key, matching the merged xAI handling in `realtime-transcription-provider.ts`) through the same shared `normalizeOptionalString` helper so blank values are treated as missing everywhere in this provider.

## Changes

- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts`: `isConfigured` and `createSession` resolve the `XI_API_KEY` fallback via `normalizeOptionalString`, so whitespace-only values report unconfigured and session creation fails fast with `ElevenLabs API key missing`.
- `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts`: the speech-to-text key resolution normalizes `req.apiKey`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `XI_API_KEY` with the same helper, so blank values are skipped and env keys are trimmed before being sent.
- Regression tests: whitespace-only env keys are treated as missing in both providers (including asserting no request is sent), and a padded env key is trimmed before use.

## User Impact

Operators with a whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`/`XI_API_KEY` (e.g., a placeholder left in an env file) now get a clear "ElevenLabs API key missing" error and the realtime provider correctly reports itself unconfigured, instead of a request sent with an empty credential that fails upstream. Real keys are unaffected (verified trimmed-to-same-value in tests). No config, migration, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/elevenlabs/` — 38/38 passed on Node 22.22.0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — no errors in changed files (only pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors from a stale local dependency install).
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Real HTTP proof below: loopback server + production functions, before/after this patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A whitespace-only `XI_API_KEY` made the realtime provider report configured, and the speech-to-text path sent a real request carrying an empty `xi-api-key` header instead of failing fast locally.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, production functions imported directly from the changed sources, real `node:http` loopback server as the ElevenLabs API endpoint (`request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` to permit the loopback target). Current head: `9acd26a1f0a75b6c328cbc951dbce3757c7109b2`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/elk-proof/proof.mts` with `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=""` and `XI_API_KEY="  "` in the environment. The driver starts a real HTTP server, calls `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured({ providerConfig: {} })`, then calls the production `transcribeElevenLabsAudio({ buffer, fileName, mime, baseUrl: <loopback>, request: { allowPrivateNetwork: true } })` and reads the server's received-request count and captured `xi-api-key` header back.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (same driver, base revision): `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): true`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: resolved (request was sent)`, `server received requests: 1`, `captured xi-api-key header: ""`. After the patch: `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): false`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: threw: ElevenLabs API key missing`, `server received requests: 0`.

**Observed result after fix:** The whitespace-only env key no longer counts as configured, the missing-key error fires locally before any network I/O (the loopback server confirms zero requests), and regression tests confirm a padded real env key (`"  env-key  "`) is trimmed and sent as `env-key`.

**What was not tested:** No live ElevenLabs API calls (no real credential available); the loopback server stands in for the upstream endpoint. The realtime websocket session path was not connected end-to-end with a blank key; its `isConfigured`/`createSession` gates are covered by the new unit tests and the same normalization helper. No UI changes.

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other providers' env credential paths (bedrock was handled in #109680, `packages/ai` env keys in #109691, deepgram in #108565); this PR is scoped to ElevenLabs only.
- The config-file `apiKey` handling, which already normalizes blanks via `normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`.
- `resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`, which already trims its env read.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock users could lose access to the AWS default credential chain when `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` was present but contained only whitespace. The AWS SDK accepts whitespace values in both its static environment credential provider and its Bedrock bearer-token environment provider, preventing fallback to profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock now trims explicitly configured bearer tokens before selecting bearer authentication. A shared credential-preparation path removes only whitespace bearer/static/session environment values before shared-config refresh and credential resolution; streaming, discovery, embeddings, and control-plane profile resolution all pass through that path.

The Mantle IAM token generation path also calls the same sanitizer before invoking the AWS SDK default credential chain, so blank static credentials cannot intercept Mantle authentication either.

The AWS SDK `fromEnv()` provider checks static values for truthiness rather than trimmed content, while `fromEnvSigningName({ signingName: "bedrock" })` accepts any present `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` value. Removing blank values lets the SDK continue through its normal default chain.

Risk note: the sanitizer mutates `process.env` for the AWS credential env vars. Every Bedrock client path (Converse stream, discovery, embeddings, inference-profile resolution, Mantle IAM) passes through credential preparation where the sanitizer runs first. Preserving nonblank values exactly and deleting only whitespace-only ones keeps the change minimal and predictable. The helper is private to each owning Bedrock provider; Mantle imports it directly in its test, not through the public api.ts barrel.

## User Impact

Users with accidentally blank Bedrock credential environment variables can continue using valid AWS profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials across streaming, model discovery, embeddings, inference-profile resolution, and Mantle IAM token generation. Valid bearer tokens and static credentials remain supported; explicitly configured bearer tokens are normalized before use.

## Evidence

**Converse + discovery + embedding credential paths (existing proof):**
- Direct production-path reproduction on Linux / Node 24.18.0: before the fix, `streamBedrock` configured the AWS client with `{"token":{"token":"   "},"authSchemePreference":["httpBearerAuth"]}` for a whitespace-only bearer token.
- Direct AWS SDK request capture before network I/O: `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` produced `Authorization: Bearer    ` from that configuration.
- After the fix, the same `streamBedrock` path configured no token provider for whitespace-only input; `"  valid-token  "` produced `{ "token": "valid-token" }`.
- Real AWS SDK default-chain proof used an isolated temporary `[default]` shared credentials file, with no network call or real credentials. Before preparation, the SDK selected both whitespace static env credentials and a whitespace Bedrock bearer env token. After preparation it removed those blank values, rejected the missing bearer env token, and resolved the temporary default profile. Redacted result: `{"beforeSelectedWhitespaceStaticEnv":true,"beforeSelectedWhitespaceBearerEnv":true,"blankEnvRemoved":true,"afterSelectedDefaultProfile":true,"blankBearerRejected":true}`.

**Mantle IAM token generation path (new proof):**
- Direct `sanitizeBlankAwsCredentials()` call from `generateBearerTokenFromIam` (`extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.ts:177`): sets whitespace-only `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, and `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, then calls the sanitizer. All four variables are deleted. Redacted output:
  ```
  === before sanitization ===
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "   "
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = "\t"
    AWS_SESSION_TOKEN = "  "
    AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK = " \t "

  === after sanitization ===
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = <deleted>
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = <deleted>
    AWS_SESSION_TOKEN = <deleted>
    AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK = <deleted>
  ```
- After blank env values are removed, the `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node` default chain rejects the (now-missing) env provider and reaches the next provider in the chain (SSO/profile/ECS/IMDS). The chain error is the expected `Could not load credentials from any providers` (no real credentials available in this test environment), not an error about blank env credentials being used.
- `sanitizeBlankAwsCredentials` is private to each owning Bedrock provider; Mantle imports it directly in `discovery.test.ts`, not through the public `api.ts` barrel.

**Test results:**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-credential-refresh.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts` — 5 files, 143 tests passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the nine PR files.
- What was not tested: live AWS credentials with real Bedrock API streaming, live Mantle IAM bearer token generation, and the Mantle IAM path end-to-end (requires AWS account with Bedrock access and IAM role).

**CI note:** The two CI failures on the rebased head (`build-artifacts` startup memory — `status --json` 428 MB median RSS vs 425 MB limit; `check-test-types` — `scripts/openclaw-npm-postpublish-verify.ts` missing `.d.ts`) are pre-existing on upstream `main` and unrelated to these Bedrock extension changes.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the streaming, discovery, embedding, provider-registration, inference-profile control-plane, and Mantle IAM token generation paths, plus the exact `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node@3.972.61`, and `@aws-sdk/token-providers` contracts.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), rejects empty bodies, and gates zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy — preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Zero-overlap update proposals are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The zero-overlap approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for zero-overlap updates while ordinary updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `92683fcb1a`**

**Terminal output from exact head** (real Skill Workshop apply flow via `node --import tsx`, 5 scenarios including incidental-overlap):

```console
=== Real Behavior Proof: Skill Workshop Apply-Body Validation ===
SHA: 92683fcb1a
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T08:28:38.286Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Zero-overlap (unrelated) update requires explicit approval ---
Original SKILL.md content:
---
name: weather
description: Weather lookup skill
---

# Weather

Steps to check weather.
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: true
Apply result.changeSummary: +4 lines, -4 lines
SKILL.md after apply contains "deploying to production": true
SKILL.md changed from original: true

--- Proof 2: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
SKILL.md before rejection:
---
name: empty-test
description: Empty test target
---

# Empty Test

Original content that must survive.
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md unchanged: true

--- Proof 3: Headingless skill update succeeds without explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -2 lines
SKILL.md contains "save the result to disk": true

--- Proof 4: Valid update with shared content succeeds ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -3 lines
SKILL.md contains "Updated steps": true
Rollback.previousContent contains "Steps to check weather": true

--- Proof 5: Incidental shared-line plan does NOT require explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +8 lines, -3 lines
Note: This proposal shares "# Weather" line but is a plan document; overlap classifier sees shared line and does not flag it as requiresExplicitApproval. The canonical parseFrontmatter validation ensures it has valid frontmatter (name, description) and non-empty body, which structurally valid plan documents do have.

=== Summary ===
1. Zero-overlap update: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
2. Empty body rejection: SKILL.md unchanged ✅
3. Headingless skill update: requiresExplicitApproval=false, succeeds ✅
4. Valid update with shared content: requiresExplicitApproval=false, changeSummary + rollback ✅
5. Incidental shared-line plan: requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected, not flagged as risky) ✅

Overlap classifier behavior:
- Zero shared lines (complete rewrite/unrelated): requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
- Any shared lines (ordinary edit or incidental overlap): requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
- Structural validation (canonical parseFrontmatter) catches empty bodies and invalid frontmatter regardless of overlap
```

**Unit tests (exact head SHA 92683fcb1a)**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts --run

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts (2 tests) 2588ms
     ✓ gates zero-overlap updates with requiresExplicitApproval and rejects empty bodies  1813ms
     ✓ applies headingless and overlapping updates without requiresExplicitApproval  769ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Validation matrix**:

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Incidental shared line (plan shares heading)    => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned, rollback recorded
```

**CI note**: The `startup-memory` check failure (`status --json` median RSS exceeding 425 MB limit) is a pre-existing issue on the `main` branch, not introduced by this PR. All other CI checks (oxlint, format, typecheck, tests, docs) passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram `/model` summary replies should preserve the rich model browse inline button so users can tap `Browse providers` instead of falling back to plain text. The previous regression test asserted the right behavior but did not register a Telegram channel-plugin fixture, so the isolated suite could not actually exercise `buildModelBrowseChannelData`.

This PR adds an explicit Telegram channel fixture for the `/model` summary test and verifies the `mdl_prov` callback payload is preserved through the same channel plugin path used by production Telegram model browsing.

## Summary

- Adds regression coverage that `/model` summary replies on Telegram preserve rich model browse `channelData`.
- Registers an explicit Telegram channel-plugin fixture for the directive test so `getChannelPlugin("telegram")` can produce the rich browse payload.
- Guards the Telegram `Browse providers` inline button contract (`mdl_prov`) so future plain-text compatibility fixes do not strip the rich browse path.

## Evidence

The live sovereign runtime patch that temporarily skipped Telegram channel data was reverted, restoring the same production path this test protects:

```js
const channelData = (params.surface ? getChannelPlugin(params.surface) : null)?.commands?.buildModelBrowseChannelData?.();
```

target.title: fix(browser): honor abortSignal during Playwright click-and-hold delay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`clickViaPlaywright`'s click-and-hold delay in `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` slept with a bare `setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)`, where `delayMs` can be up to `ACT_MAX_CLICK_DELAY_MS = 5_000` (`act-policy.ts:22`). The interaction `AbortSignal` is already in scope and is checked via `throwIfInteractionAborted(signal)` right before and after the sleep — but the sleep itself was not abortable.

When the signal fires mid-hold, the caller-visible promise does reject promptly (the `abortPromise` race in `awaitActionWithAbort`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts:488`), but the *action chain* is orphaned: the ref'd 5 s timer keeps sleeping after the caller is gone, then throws at the post-delay check. While orphaned it pins the event loop for the remainder of the hold, and it delays the navigation-guard teardown that only runs after the action settles — the delayed-navigation observation plus the 250 ms grace and the final `assertPageNavigationCompletedSafely` (`pw-tools-core.interactions.ts:569-590`), and with an SSRF policy active the `page.route("**")` interception installed by `withPageNavigationRequestGuard` (`pw-session.ts:1663`) stays attached to the tab for the rest of the hold as well.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hold is now `await sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` (`packages/retry/src/index.ts:21`, re-exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, already imported elsewhere in this plugin, e.g. `sleep` in `cdp.helpers.ts`). `sleepWithAbort` clears its timer and rejects on abort, so the orphaned chain unwinds at the abort event instead of after the full remaining delay. The pre/post `throwIfInteractionAborted(signal)` checks are unchanged, so behavior with no signal or no abort is identical.

The surfaced error is unchanged: `clickViaPlaywright` registers its abort listener (which rejects the race with `signal.reason`) before the action starts, so the race still rejects with the original abort reason — the proof below shows byte-identical rejection messages before and after. No new config, no new env, no SDK surface change.

Pattern reference: #108561 (merged) did the same `setTimeout` → `sleepWithAbort` swap for the Discord gateway READY backoff. Sibling #109617 covers the browser tab-discovery poll; this PR covers the click-and-hold hold delay — disjoint code paths.

## User Impact

- Cancelling an agent browser click with a hold delay (e.g. a 5 s click-and-hold) no longer leaves an orphaned action chain sleeping in the background: the timer is cleared at the abort event and the event loop can drain ~immediately (proof: 5010 ms → 338 ms).
- The post-interaction navigation guard (delayed-navigation observation, grace window, final safety recheck, and request interception when an SSRF policy is configured) is released at the abort instead of up to 5 s later, so follow-up interactions on the same tab no longer run under a stale, aborted interaction's guard state.
- Happy path is untouched: without an abort the click still waits the full `delayMs` before dispatching (locked by regression test).

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool opts | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 708 | `const signal = opts.signal` |
| Abort race | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 713-740 | `abortPromise` rejects with `signal.reason`; listener registered before the action runs |
| Hold delay (this PR) | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 758 | `await sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` — timer cleared + rejection on abort |
| Sleep impl | `packages/retry/src/index.ts` | 21 | `sleepWithAbort`: `clearTimeout` + `reject(new Error("aborted", { cause: signal.reason }))` on the abort event |
| Race | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 488-506 | `Promise.race([actionPromise, abortPromise])`; late action rejection swallowed to avoid unhandled rejections |
| Guard teardown | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 569-590 | grace + `assertPageNavigationCompletedSafely` run in `finally` once the action settles — now reached at abort time |

### Real behavior proof — production `clickViaPlaywright`, real `AbortController`, wall-clock

Uncommitted proof script drives the production `clickViaPlaywright` (`resolvedPage` stub whose `locator()` returns an observed locator, `selector` + `delayMs: 5000`, no CDP connection), aborts 100 ms into the 5 000 ms hold, then measures `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` Timeout entries and the `beforeExit` timestamp (when the event loop could actually drain). No mocks, no vitest.

**Before fix (main @ 9638c3ae07)**

```json
{
  "delayMs": 5000,
  "abortAtMs": 100,
  "events": [["hover", 2], ["abort()", 106], ["settled", 149]],
  "callerRejected": true,
  "rejectionMessage": "proof: user cancelled click-and-hold",
  "rejectElapsedMs": 149,
  "hoverFired": true,
  "clickFired": false,
  "timeoutResourcesAfterReject": 1,
  "eventLoopDrainedAtMs": 5010,
  "verdict": "BUG: caller rejected but the orphaned hold-delay timer pins the event loop for the full 5000ms"
}
```

**After fix (this PR)**

```json
{
  "delayMs": 5000,
  "abortAtMs": 100,
  "events": [["hover", 4], ["abort()", 106], ["settled", 138]],
  "callerRejected": true,
  "rejectionMessage": "proof: user cancelled click-and-hold",
  "rejectElapsedMs": 138,
  "hoverFired": true,
  "clickFired": false,
  "timeoutResourcesAfterReject": 0,
  "eventLoopDrainedAtMs": 338,
  "verdict": "FIXED: abort clears the hold-delay timer; event loop drains right after the abort"
}
```

Every field is independently checkable: `timeoutResourcesAfterReject` counts `"Timeout"` entries in `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` after the caller already rejected (1 = the orphaned 5 000 ms sleep; 0 = cleared by the abort), and `eventLoopDrainedAtMs` is the `process.beforeExit` timestamp relative to t0. The rejection message is byte-identical before/after — the abort-reason error surface is unchanged.

### Control-red (mutation) verification

The new regression test fails on the unpatched code and passes on this branch:

| Version | `unwinds the hold-delay action chain promptly when aborted mid-delay` | `still waits the full hold delay before clicking when not aborted` |
|---|---|---|
| main @ 9638c3ae07 | **fails** — post-abort navigation recheck still pending 1 000 ms after the abort (orphan sleeps the full 5 000 ms first) | passes |
| this PR | **passes** — recheck completes within the 250 ms observation + 250 ms grace after the abort | passes |

Revert is exactly the production hunk above (`sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` → bare `setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)`); no test edits between runs.

### Regression test

`extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.click-delay.abort.test.ts` (colocated, uses the shared `pw-tools-core.test-harness.ts` mocks): aborts a real `AbortController` 100 ms into a 5 000 ms hold and asserts (a) rejection with the original abort reason, (b) `locator.click` never fires, (c) the existing force-disconnect-on-abort call still happens with `reason: "click aborted"`, and (d) the orphaned chain's navigation recheck settles promptly instead of after the full hold. Second test locks the happy path: without abort, the click fires only after the full 5 000 ms.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.click-delay.abort.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.navigation-guard.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.evaluate.abort.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.batch.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.set-input-files.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.click-delay.abort.test.ts
(exit 0, no findings)
```

### tsgo

```
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json
(exit 0, 0 errors)
```

target.title: fix(qqbot): align typing lifecycle with core TypingController
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

  Fixes an issue where QQ Bot C2C users would see the "typing…" indicator driven by a self-built interval timer
  (TypingKeepAlive) that started and stopped independently of the model's actual inference and reply dispatch state. The
  typing cue could drift out of sync with the real reply progress (running too long after the reply was sent, or
  stopping early during long tool calls), and the keep-alive loop had to be hand-stopped at every early-return and
  finally-block in the gateway, creating fragile stop-site bookkeeping.

  Resolves the mismatch by wiring QQ typing into the OpenClaw core TypingController lifecycle, the same seam Telegram
  uses, so typing start/stop is precise to model onReplyStart and dispatch-idle.

  ## Why This Change Was Made

  The self-built TypingKeepAlive duplicated the core typing lifecycle's interval/in-flight-suppression logic and
  required manual stop() calls scattered across gateway.ts and outbound-dispatch.ts. This replaces it with
  createChannelMessageReplyPipeline + TypingController (via typingCallbacks in dispatcherOptions), so the core
  controller owns start (onReplyStart), keepalive refresh, and cleanup (markRunComplete + markDispatchIdle).

  Key design decisions and non-goals:

  - QQ's distinct typing model is preserved: input_second=10 display window with a 5s refresh interval
    (keepaliveIntervalMs, explicitly set rather than the core's 3s default so consecutive ticks overlap seamlessly), and
    every typing tick still spends one of QQ's 5-per-msg_id passive-reply slots — unlike Telegram's budget-free
    heartbeat.

  - typing-callbacks.ts owns the QQ-specific per-tick send: claimMessageReply(msgId, 1) reserves one passive slot for
    the final text reply; when only the reserved slot remains, the tick falls back to a proactive input_notify without
    msg_id so it never starves the final reply. One token-refresh retry; maxConsecutiveFailures=3.

  - gateway.startTypingForEvent now sends only the early input_notify cue (mirroring Telegram's early typing cue) and
    returns refIdx for quote resolution — no keepalive loop.

  - InboundContext.typing field and all keepAlive.stop() call sites are removed; the core controller is the single stop
    signal.

  - Non-goal: changing the passive-reply budget (still 5/hour) or the proactive-fallback behavior in
    sender.ts/streaming-c2c.ts.

  ## User Impact

  QQ Bot C2C users now see a "typing…" indicator that starts precisely when the model begins generating and stops as
  soon as the reply is dispatched — no more lingering indicators after the message lands, and no premature cutoff during
  long tool-augmented replies. Long-running turns are also safer: typing can no longer accidentally consume the last
  passive-reply slot, so the final text reply always gets through (falling back to a proactive message only when the
  hourly budget is genuinely exhausted).

  For group/guild messages, behavior is unchanged (no typing indicator, as before).

  ## Evidence

  - Tests: 669 qqbot tests pass (81 files), including 9 new typing-callbacks.test.ts tests covering per-tick budget
    claim (reserve=1), proactive fallback when only the reserved slot remains, token-refresh retry, non-token-error no-
    retry, and 3 budget-protection tests proving the final reply's passive slot survives typing ticks (including a
    simulated in-flight residual tick).

  - Delivery-trace goldens: Regenerated all 5 goldens. The new wire recording shows the core controller firing
    input_notify on onReplyStart (one extra passive spend per C2C scenario) and keepalive ticks every 5s; budget-
    exhaustion.trace.jsonl now demonstrates the proactive fallback (typing ticks at at=15000/at=20000 send without
    msg_id once the passive budget is reserved-exhausted, and only the first of five message-tool replies keeps msg_id).
    EXPECTED_REPLY_BUDGET_REMAINING updated accordingly (streaming-happy-c2c: 3→2, media-interrupt: 1→0, budget-
    exhaustion: 0).

  - Static checks: tsgo typecheck clean (production tsconfig.extensions.json + tsconfig.extensions.test.json), oxlint
    clean, oxfmt applied, git diff --check clean.

  - Note: $autoreview could not run in this environment (Codex engine returned 401 Unauthorized against
    wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses — environment auth, not a code issue); validation was completed via the test suite
    + typecheck/lint/format above.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), rejects empty bodies, and gates zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy — preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Zero-overlap update proposals are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The zero-overlap approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for zero-overlap updates while ordinary updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `92683fcb1a`**

**Terminal output from exact head** (real Skill Workshop apply flow via `node --import tsx`, 5 scenarios including incidental-overlap):

```console
=== Real Behavior Proof: Skill Workshop Apply-Body Validation ===
SHA: 92683fcb1a
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T08:28:38.286Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Zero-overlap (unrelated) update requires explicit approval ---
Original SKILL.md content:
---
name: weather
description: Weather lookup skill
---

# Weather

Steps to check weather.
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: true
Apply result.changeSummary: +4 lines, -4 lines
SKILL.md after apply contains "deploying to production": true
SKILL.md changed from original: true

--- Proof 2: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
SKILL.md before rejection:
---
name: empty-test
description: Empty test target
---

# Empty Test

Original content that must survive.
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md unchanged: true

--- Proof 3: Headingless skill update succeeds without explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -2 lines
SKILL.md contains "save the result to disk": true

--- Proof 4: Valid update with shared content succeeds ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -3 lines
SKILL.md contains "Updated steps": true
Rollback.previousContent contains "Steps to check weather": true

--- Proof 5: Incidental shared-line plan does NOT require explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +8 lines, -3 lines
Note: This proposal shares "# Weather" line but is a plan document; overlap classifier sees shared line and does not flag it as requiresExplicitApproval. The canonical parseFrontmatter validation ensures it has valid frontmatter (name, description) and non-empty body, which structurally valid plan documents do have.

=== Summary ===
1. Zero-overlap update: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
2. Empty body rejection: SKILL.md unchanged ✅
3. Headingless skill update: requiresExplicitApproval=false, succeeds ✅
4. Valid update with shared content: requiresExplicitApproval=false, changeSummary + rollback ✅
5. Incidental shared-line plan: requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected, not flagged as risky) ✅

Overlap classifier behavior:
- Zero shared lines (complete rewrite/unrelated): requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
- Any shared lines (ordinary edit or incidental overlap): requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
- Structural validation (canonical parseFrontmatter) catches empty bodies and invalid frontmatter regardless of overlap
```

**Unit tests (exact head SHA 92683fcb1a)**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts --run

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts (2 tests) 2588ms
     ✓ gates zero-overlap updates with requiresExplicitApproval and rejects empty bodies  1813ms
     ✓ applies headingless and overlapping updates without requiresExplicitApproval  769ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Validation matrix**:

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Incidental shared line (plan shares heading)    => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned, rollback recorded
```

**CI note**: The `startup-memory` check failure (`status --json` median RSS exceeding 425 MB limit) is a pre-existing issue on the `main` branch, not introduced by this PR. All other CI checks (oxlint, format, typecheck, tests, docs) passed.

target.title: fix(telegram): stop draft-stream final flush promptly when discarded during retry_after wait
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`stop()` in `extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts:667` gates its final flush on Telegram's `retry_after` flood window via `waitForRetryAfter()` (`draft-stream.ts:669-676`), which sleeps on a bare `setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)` (line 673). The `stopped` flag is only re-checked *after* the sleep completes (lines 686, 700), so when the stream is torn down mid-wait — `clear()`/`discard()` via `stopForClear`, e.g. a superseded reply turn (`bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts:449`), a text-deliverer discard (`lane-delivery-text-deliverer.ts:241`), or a terminal preview failure (`draft-stream.ts:538`) — the parked `stop()` keeps sleeping out the rest of the window even though the final text will never be delivered. The window is capped at `MAX_PREVIEW_FLOOD_SUSPEND_MS = 60_000` (line 53) per wait, and `stop()` waits once before the initial flush (line 685) plus up to twice in the bounded resume loop (line 699), so a discard during the final flush can leave the reply turn parked for tens of seconds (worst case ~120s+), delaying the reply turn's teardown while the account is stopping.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wait is now stop-aware. `streamState.stopped` transitions abort a per-stream `AbortController`, and `waitForRetryAfter` races the window against that signal with `sleepWithAbort` (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`) — the same helper and pattern as the merged sibling fix in this extension (#109604, `probe.ts:197`) and #108561 (discord). The interception lives on the `streamState` accessor because teardown marks `stopped` through the shared SDK controls state (`stopForClear` → `markStopped`, `src/channels/draft-stream-controls.ts:92-97`); catching the write at the state object covers the SDK path and the three local `stopped = true` sites (lines 449, 538, 899) in one place without touching shared channel code. The controller re-arms when the stream resets to a new message (`resetStreamToNewMessage`, line 744), so later turns still honor fresh flood windows. On wake, the existing `generation !== stopGeneration || streamState.stopped` re-checks own the early return, exactly as before.

Scope discipline — deliberately unchanged:

- `MAX_PREVIEW_FLOOD_SUSPEND_MS` (60s cap) and the `retry_after` bookkeeping.
- The 2-attempt bounded resume loop and all existing early-return checks.
- Graceful-path behavior: a non-discarded `stop()` still waits the full `retry_after` before sending (rate-limit compliance).
- The detached delete scheduling (`scheduleDetachedDelete`, line ~797), which is fire-and-forget by design and never stalls teardown.

No new config, no new env, no SDK or shared-core change: 1 source file, +27/-4 lines.

## User Impact

Discarding or clearing a Telegram draft stream while its final flush is parked behind a `retry_after` window now lets `stop()` return immediately instead of holding the reply turn (and account teardown) for up to ~60s per remaining wait. Rate-limit compliance is unchanged for graceful stops: the full window is still honored before the final edit is attempted.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — production `stop()` path, real wall-clock timers

Uncommitted `scratchpad/draft-stream-stop-aware-retry-wait.mts` drives the real `createTelegramDraftStream` through its public `api` seam (no module mocks, no fake timers). A real 429-shaped `editMessageText` rejection (`error_code: 429, parameters: { retry_after: 5 }`) arms the suspension through the production `readTelegramRetryAfterMs` path; `stop()` starts its final flush and `discard()` (the teardown path used by `cleanup(superseded)`) fires at +200ms.

**Before** (origin/main @ e01027dd28):

```json
{
  "discardRun":  { "scenario": "discard-mid-wait", "stopElapsedMs": 5005, "finalEditDelivered": false },
  "gracefulRun": { "scenario": "graceful", "stopElapsedMs": 5007, "finalEditDelivered": true,
                   "editCalls": [{ "atMs": 1, "text": "Hello again" }, { "atMs": 5009, "text": "Hello final" }] }
}
PARKED: stop() stayed behind the retry_after window for 5005ms despite discard at +200ms
OK: graceful stop() honored the window (5007ms)
```

**After** (this PR):

```json
{
  "discardRun":  { "scenario": "discard-mid-wait", "stopElapsedMs": 201, "finalEditDelivered": false },
  "gracefulRun": { "scenario": "graceful", "stopElapsedMs": 5006, "finalEditDelivered": true,
                   "editCalls": [{ "atMs": 0, "text": "Hello again" }, { "atMs": 5007, "text": "Hello final" }] }
}
OK: stop() returned 201ms after discard at +200ms
OK: graceful stop() honored the window (5006ms)
```

Same script, same harness: discard-mid-wait drops 5005ms → 201ms (≈ the +200ms discard point), no final edit is attempted after discard, and the graceful run still waits the full ~5000ms window and delivers the final text at 5007ms — retry_after compliance preserved.

### Control-red (mutation) verification

`git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts` (keeping the new tests) →

- `returns stop's final flush promptly when discarded during the retry_after wait` **fails** immediately: `expect(stopSettled).toBe(true)` receives `false` — the wait stays parked on the bare timer.
- `honors a new retry_after window after a discarded stream resets` **hangs** at `await firstStop` — the pre-fix code cannot leave the window without the fake clock advancing, which is exactly the parking behavior under test.

Restoring the fix makes both pass.

### Regression coverage

- New: `returns stop's final flush promptly when discarded during the retry_after wait` — discard mid-wait settles `stop()` without advancing the fake clock into the window; the final text is never sent.
- New: `honors a new retry_after window after a discarded stream resets` — after discard + `forceNewMessage()`, a fresh suspension still gates `stop()` for the full window (guards the controller re-arm; without it the resumed stream would skip `retry_after`).
- Existing: `gates stop's initial final flush on an existing retry_after window` and the bounded-resume pagination tests continue to lock the graceful path.

### Validation

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts
# Test Files  1 passed (1) — Tests 86 passed (86)

oxlint extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts
# exit=0

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json
# exit=0

git diff --check origin/main
# clean
```

target.title: fix(coding-agent): isolate Codex CLI CODEX_HOME from OpenClaw OAuth in skill launch forms
target.body:
Closes #109704

AI-assisted: built with Codex

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the bundled `coding-agent` skill's documented Codex CLI
launch forms use the ambient `CODEX_HOME` (`~/.codex` default), which can share
the same ChatGPT OAuth credential with OpenClaw's own `openai` provider.
When both clients use the same account's refresh token, one client can consume
or rotate the token, causing the other to fail with `refresh_token_reused`.
This leaves OpenClaw unable to make model requests until manual re-authentication.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `coding-agent` skill's documented `codex exec` launch forms now scope
Codex CLI to a dedicated `CODEX_HOME` kept **outside** every Git worktree so it
never discovers the ambient `~/.codex` credential and never places OAuth
credentials (`auth.json`) inside a checkout the coding worker may commit from.

Three locations are updated:

- **Hard rule**: instructs operators to create a `CODEX_HOME` outside every Git
  worktree (`mkdir -p <safe-path> && chmod 700 <safe-path>`), authenticate once,
  and prepend it to every `codex exec` launch. Warns that `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json`
  must never be staged or committed.
- **Codex launch form**: uses `/safe/path/.codex-isolated` instead of a
  worktree-relative path.
- **Scratch Codex**: allocates a dedicated `mktemp -d` directory outside
  `$SCRATCH` with mode 700 instead of creating `.codex-home` inside the scratch
  repo.

The runtime's bounded-turn path already isolates `CODEX_HOME`; this fix brings
the skill's manual launch forms into alignment with a safe external-home
convention.

## User Impact

Users who authenticate both OpenClaw and Codex CLI with the same ChatGPT
account no longer risk OpenClaw OAuth breakage when the `coding-agent` skill
launches a Codex worker. Codex credentials and session state are never placed
inside a Git checkout.

## Evidence

Runtime already isolates CODEX_HOME in the bounded-turn path:

```
extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.ts:101  codexHome = path.join(workspace.dir, "codex-home")
extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.ts:282  CODEX_HOME: codexHome
```

Skill launch forms before this change (ambient `~/.codex`):

```
bash ... command:"codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Skill launch forms after this change (scoped, external, mode 700):

```
bash ... command:"CODEX_HOME=/safe/path/.codex-isolated codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Scratch Codex before (CODEX_HOME inside git repo):

```
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/.codex-home"
... command:"codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Scratch Codex after (CODEX_HOME outside git repo, mode 700):

```
CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d)
chmod 700 "$CODEX_HOME"
... command:"CODEX_HOME=$CODEX_HOME codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Docs-only change; no runtime behavior, tests, or build output affected.

target.title: fix(scripts): preserve emoji in realtime smoke diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Google Live realtime-talk smoke diagnostics when an incoming WebSocket frame reaches the 300-code-unit preview boundary at an emoji. It also keeps the final frame visible when an abnormal close follows immediately after a message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Live event payloads are external text and can contain arbitrary Unicode. The original page-side `slice(0, 300)` could cut a surrogate pair before the debug snapshot was serialized. An initial host callback avoided that cut but introduced an asynchronous gap between the message and close handlers.

The final implementation sets browser frames to `arraybuffer`, captures a bounded structured snapshot synchronously before parsing, and returns failures as data. It retains at most eight complete messages up to 16 Ki UTF-16 code units each; oversized frames are replaced wholesale with a content-free length marker, so structured secrets are never cut before redaction. Node then applies the existing dev-tool redactor and UTF-16-safe preview to complete retained messages and close reasons before constructing the diagnostic.

## User Impact

Realtime-talk smoke failures now preserve message ordering and report bounded, redacted, valid-Unicode diagnostics at emoji boundaries.

## Evidence

- Exact head `5a302aee5b1`, rebased once onto latest submission-time `main` `e3618454f24`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/dev-tooling-safety.test.ts` on Node 24.15.0: 64 tests passed after the rebase.
- Final abnormal-close diagnostic regression covers a 296-code-unit prefix followed by an emoji and verifies no emoji tail leaks.
- Structured-secret regression verifies redaction runs before the 300-code-unit preview.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh pre-submit autoreview reported no actionable findings.

target.title: fix(browser): honor AbortSignal in tab discovery poll
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`waitForTabDiscoveryPoll` in `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.selection.ts:67-71` slept the full `OPEN_TAB_DISCOVERY_POLL_MS = 100` between tab-discovery poll attempts using a bare `setTimeout(resolve, OPEN_TAB_DISCOVERY_POLL_MS)` that never received the owning `ensureTabAvailable` `AbortSignal`. When a caller aborts mid-poll (for example, a route timeout or a higher-level cancellation), the loop sits through the remainder of the 100 ms delay before the next `readTabs` call notices the aborted signal.

The poll loop is entered for local-managed profiles when a tab lacks a `wsUrl` and `supportsPerTabWs` is true (server-context.selection.ts:149-167). Sibling abort points around it already honor the signal: `ensureBrowserAvailable({ signal: options?.signal })` at line 92 and `options?.signal?.throwIfAborted()` inside `readTabs` at line 109. Only the poll sleep itself was unwired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The poll sleep is now `sleepWithAbort(OPEN_TAB_DISCOVERY_POLL_MS, signal)`, the same helper already used by sibling Browser code and by Telegram/Discord/Zalo monitors. `sleepWithAbort` (`packages/retry/src/index.ts:21`) rejects on abort, so cancellation propagates out of `ensureTabAvailable` immediately instead of waiting for the poll window to elapse.

The helper signature stays internal and backward-compatible: `waitForTabDiscoveryPoll` now accepts an optional `AbortSignal`, and the existing caller passes `options?.signal`. No other callers exist, and `undefined` preserves the original sleep behavior.

No new config, no new env var, no SDK change, no shared-helper change.

## User Impact

Cancelling a browser operation while `ensureTabAvailable` is polling for a tab's WebSocket URL no longer holds the call for the remainder of the 100 ms poll interval. The loop exits on the next abort event, matching the responsiveness already provided by the surrounding `ensureBrowserAvailable` and `readTabs` checks. Happy-path behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Fix before (mutation proof)**

Reverting only the production change while keeping the new regression test:

```
FAIL  |extension-browser| extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-discovery-poll-abort.test.ts
AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error matching /aborted/i but got 'tab not found'
Duration: 2231ms
```

The original code waited the full poll delay repeatedly until the 2000 ms discovery window expired, then surfaced `BrowserTabNotFoundError` instead of honoring the abort.

**Fix after**

```
PASS  |extension-browser| extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-discovery-poll-abort.test.ts
Duration: 7.26s (transform 3.75s, setup 653ms, import 6.14s, tests 145ms)
```

The regression test uses a real `AbortController`, a local-managed profile, and a mocked `listTabs` that returns a tab without `wsUrl`. Once the poll loop starts, it aborts the signal and asserts that `ensureTabAvailable` rejects with an `aborted` error in well under `OPEN_TAB_DISCOVERY_POLL_MS / 2`.

**Focused checks**

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-discovery-poll-abort.test.ts` passed
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-selection-state.test.ts` passed (36/36)
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.existing-session.test.ts` passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` exit=0

target.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite startup falls back to the system `mount` command when `/proc/self/mountinfo` is unavailable. That synchronous probe had no deadline, so a stalled `mount` process could block state or plugin database initialization indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback probe now has a one-second hard timeout. If filesystem classification times out, SQLite conservatively uses rollback journaling instead of assuming WAL is safe. Existing behavior for successful mount classification and non-timeout probe failures is preserved.

## User Impact

Database-backed OpenClaw startup no longer waits indefinitely on a wedged mount probe. When the deadline is reached, startup continues with rollback journaling, avoiding both the hang and an unsafe WAL assumption for an unclassified network filesystem.

## Evidence

- Regression-first tests cover the missing timeout and the conservative timeout policy.
- Before: the production `configureSqliteWalMaintenance` path with an isolated stalled `mount` fixture exceeded a 4-second external guard (`exit_status=124`).
- After: the same production path returned in about 1.0 seconds, selected `journal_mode=delete`, and exited successfully.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts` on Node 24.15.0: 38 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts`: passed.
- Type-aware oxlint and TypeScript checking for the affected files: passed.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: no actionable findings after the conservative rollback follow-up.

Not exercised: a real macOS/BSD host or a real network filesystem. The live proof used the production SQLite configuration call path with a test-only local command fixture.

target.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

## Summary

- Complete the existing Control UI MCP App host bridge with safe, text-only `ui/message` support routed through the normal visible chat-send path.
- Advertise messaging only for fresh, authorized app views; reconstructed views remain explicitly read-only.
- Propagate live theme and iframe dimensions through the official MCP Apps host-context bridge without remounting, with observer/listener cleanup on teardown.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI could render MCP App resources and service app tool/resource requests, but an app could not safely ask the user to send plain text through the host chat, and mounted apps did not receive live theme or size changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the already-present iframe/resource reconstruction architecture. It reuses the existing widget-prompt validation and `WIDGET_PROMPT_EVENT` send seam, adds host-owned exact-text confirmation for MCP App requests, and uses the official `AppBridge.setHostContext` lifecycle. It does not add a second send route, config/env surface, protocol version, or privileged approval path.

The implementation adds a small explicit `readOnly` lease marker because a fresh app may legitimately have zero app-callable tools, while a transcript-reconstructed preview must remain resource-only. Tool-count inference could not represent both states safely.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, a visible and focused fresh app can request that the user send one plain-text message. The host shows the exact text for confirmation, then sends through the existing chat composer path. Hidden/background frames, empty or oversized text, slash commands, and rate-limit excesses are rejected. Apps also receive current theme and dimensions as they change.

## Independent landing and backward safety

- The gateway response field is additive. Older Control UIs ignore it; a newer UI talking to an older gateway sees the field absent and installs/advertises no message handler.
- Existing widget prompts use the same extracted validation/send helper without the MCP App confirmation callback; their existing behavior is covered by the widget-prompt and tool-card regression suites.
- App tool/resource handlers, app-only policy, sandbox origins, inner opaque iframe isolation, routes, config, and protocol versions are unchanged.
- Fresh views with an explicit authority set may advertise messaging even when that set is empty. Legacy views without authority and reconstructed `readOnly` views fail closed.
- No behavior enabled by this PR requires a later MCP Apps PR.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: all behavior remains behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Within that gate, `message.text` is advertised only when a fresh view has explicit current-run authority and the host handler is installed. Reconstructed views can still render/read resources but cannot message or call tools. Rich or multi-block `ui/message` content is intentionally unsupported.

## Evidence

- Genuine browser flow: a browser-bundled `App` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` ran through the real Control UI Vite app, dedicated sandbox HTTP server, and nested iframe bridge. The official initialize handshake advertised `message.text`; exact host consent was required; accepted text produced the normal `chat.send` request (`deliver: false`); the app received its response; live light-theme and container-dimension changes propagated without remounting.
- Focused exact-patch Testbox proof: 71/71 assertions passed across MCP view leases, transcript reconstruction, gateway authorization, text/focus/visibility/size/rate/slash boundaries, existing widget prompts, host-context updates, and cleanup.
- Production build passed, including the Control UI lazy chunk (`mcp-app-view-registration`, 63.20 kB) and Control UI performance limits.
- Changed-surface checks passed through formatting, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and related policy gates. An earlier Plugin SDK baseline mismatch was independently reproduced on untouched canonical main; the current canonical base includes its unrelated generated/declaration repairs.
- A first CI run exposed a production lint suppression for the SDK's request-style `onmessage` setter. The handler now registers through the SDK's exported `McpUiMessageRequestSchema`; the component and suppression-ratchet tests pass, followed by two clean fresh autoreviews.
- Two fresh full-branch autoreviews after the final safety fixes reported no actionable findings. Later canonical-base rebases were patch-identical by `git range-diff`; the last review was clean at confidence 0.88.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.widget-prompts.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:changed -- src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.ts` (all relevant checks green; unrelated main-only SDK baseline mismatch noted above)
- `pnpm build`
- Fresh `$autoreview` passes before and after simplification/final safety edits

## Simplification and scope

The PR changes five production files and four focused test files. Net production growth is +68 LOC: the new schema-registered handler/host-context lifecycle and explicit read-only authority marker are offset by deleting the duplicated widget-prompt policy/send implementation. No additional abstraction module, route, config, or compatibility shim was added.

## Known gaps

- This does not enable MCP Apps globally or implement later rollout work.
- Only one plain text content block is accepted; rich content remains rejected.
- Transcript-reconstructed previews intentionally remain read-only until a fresh run grants current authority.

target.title: fix(cli): write --json payloads to stdout not stderr
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
`openclaw node identity --json`, `promos list --json`, `daemon restart --safe --json`, and `tasks show <id> --json` emitted their JSON result to STDERR, leaving stdout empty — breaking `| jq` and any programmatic consumer (exit 0, empty stdout).

## Why This Change Was Made
--json mode redirects console.* to stderr (json-output-mode.ts) to keep incidental diagnostics off stdout. These four sites emitted the actual payload via runtime.log() (console.log), so it got swept to stderr too. They now use writeRuntimeJson (process.stdout.write), matching health/tasks-list/capability. Human (non-json) output unchanged.

## User Impact
--json output from these commands is now valid JSON on stdout, pipeable to jq. No change to interactive output.

## Evidence
Regression tests assert JSON on stdout (not stderr) for node-identity and promos-list. 25 tests pass; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` green.
